### Overview

The `ereport` function is a central component of error reporting within PostgreSQL’s backend C-code infrastructure. It acts as an abstraction layer responsible for generating and emitting log messages or errors that can be written to server logs or displayed back to clients when something goes wrong.

To help you effectively navigate this part of the codebase, understanding where `ereport` gets called from—and how—are important first steps.

#### Error Reporting System (`backend/utils/errcodes.h`)

- `elog`: Core logging macro which wraps around `ereport`.
- `ereport`: Main function responsible for constructing error reports.

In general terms, any point at which an error condition arises will use one of these abstractions to construct a message and send it through appropriate channels depending on severity level and context.
